blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Debits and credits are the two sides of every accounting entry. They sound mysterious at first, but the rule is simple. Every transaction has at least one debit and at least one credit, and the two must be equal.

For an asset account, like cash, a debit makes it go up and a credit makes it go down. For a liability account, like a loan, it is the opposite. A credit makes it go up, and a debit makes it go down.

The rule feels backwards at first, but it becomes natural with practice. For now, just remember: every entry has two sides, and the two sides are always equal.

items.q: How many sides does every accounting entry have?
items.why: "Debits and credits are the two sides of every accounting entry."

items.q: For an asset account like cash, what does a debit do?
items.why: "For an asset account, like cash, a debit makes it go up."

items.q: The text says the two sides of an entry must be…
items.why: "the two must be equal." Os dois lados sempre são iguais.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which sentence?
options: The rule is hard to learn and never gets easier.
Practice makes the rule feel natural.
Debits and credits must be equal.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que a regra "becomes natural with practice", então o autor discorda que ela nunca fica fácil.

items.q: The text suggests that, at first, the rule…
items.why: Inferência: "The rule feels backwards at first" — no começo parece estranho, depois fica natural.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry explicando os débitos e créditos a um novo trainee. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, don't be nervous. This is easier than it looks. Let me show you one small example.

A customer buys some coffee and pays us in cash. That is one transaction. So we make one entry, and every entry has two sides.

First, cash goes up. Cash is an asset, so we write a debit. The debit is one hundred dollars. Now the other side. We made a sale, so we write a credit for one hundred dollars too.

Look at the two numbers. One debit, one hundred. One credit, one hundred. They are equal. That is the rule. The debit and the credit must always match.

I know it feels backwards at first. Everybody feels that way on the first day. But you will do it many times, and soon it will feel natural. With a little practice, you will not even think about it.

Here is my simple test for you. After every entry, stop and check one thing. Do the debits equal the credits? If yes, good. If no, something is wrong, and we look again.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does the customer buy in Harry's example?
items.why: "A customer buys some coffee and pays us in cash."

items.q: How much is the debit for cash?
items.why: "The debit is one hundred dollars."

items.q: What is Harry's simple test after every entry?
options: Check if the debits equal the credits
items.why: "Do the debits equal the credits? If yes, good."

items.q: Why does Harry say "everybody feels that way on the first day"?
options: Because the rule feels strange to new people at first
items.why: Inferência: ele fala logo depois de "it feels backwards at first" — é normal achar estranho no começo.

items.q: How does Harry treat the nervous trainee?
items.why: Inferência: ele diz "don't be nervous", dá um exemplo pequeno e um teste simples — é paciente e ajuda.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We write one debit and one credit for the sale." A debit is…
options: one side of an accounting entry
items.why: Debit = débito, um dos dois lados de um lançamento.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Every ___ has two sides, a debit and a credit."
items.why: Entry = lançamento; cada lançamento tem dois lados.

items.q: "For a loan, it is the opposite: a credit makes it go up." Opposite means…
items.why: Opposite = oposto, o contrário.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The two sides must be ___, not different."
items.why: Equal = igual; os dois lados sempre são iguais.

items.q: "With a little practice, the rule feels easy." Practice means…
options: doing something many times to get better
items.why: Practice = prática; fazer muitas vezes para melhorar.

blocks.instruction: Expressões simples que aparecem no trabalho de contabilidade. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The numbers do not match, so we have to look again." To look again means to…
items.why: Look again = olhar de novo, verificar mais uma vez.

items.q: "The debit and the credit must always match." To match means to…
items.why: Match = combinar, ser igual; os dois lados têm o mesmo valor.

items.q: "Cash goes up when we make a sale." To go up means to…
items.why: Go up = subir, aumentar.

items.q: "Let me show you a small example." To show someone means to…
options: help them see or understand something
items.why: Show you = mostrar, ajudar a ver e entender.

items.q: "If the sides are not equal, something is wrong." Wrong means…
items.why: Wrong = errado, não correto.
